title: GitHub Trending Today #58: herdr-app, Raven, rerun, cinecode, terminal-mac, latch, gputaskman

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending today number 58. 35 trending open source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.

sections.title: herdr-app
paragraphs: Herder is a desktop app for running your terminals and coding agents in one window written in Rust on top of Ghosty's terminal engine. Group your work into spaces, then tabs and panes. A sidebar lists every agent and shows whether it's working, blocked, done, or idle, so you know which one needs you next. Close the window and your terminals keep running in the background.

sections.title: Claude-Code-Game-Studios
paragraphs: Claude Code Game Studios gives your game project a whole team of AI specialists. It comes with agents for game design, programming, art, audio, and testing, organized like a studio with leads and directors. Slashcomands guide you from brainstorming through development and release with dedicated agents for god do unity and unreal. You can also choose how much process and review your project needs.

sections.title: Raven
paragraphs: Raven is a lightweight guey library written in C for building editors and tools drawing everything with Vulcan and running natively on Windows, Linux and Mac OS. You lay out your interface in XML, then load it from your code, hook up the actions and grab widgets by name. It has docking panels, a code editor with syntax highlighting, and frosted glass effects.

sections.title: rerun
paragraphs: Rerun lets you set up a team of AI co-workers to handle recurring tasks. Tell it what you need, and it helps create agents with their own jobs, skills, and memory. They can use connected tools, run on a schedule, and ask for approval before sending, paying, or deleting. You can watch their work on a shared board, and even host the whole thing yourself.

sections.title: cinecode
paragraphs: Cynicode is an open kit that lets an AI coding agent like Claude Code or Cursor make a whole short film from the script to the final MP4. You describe your idea, answer a few questions, and approve a plan and storyboard. Then the agent builds every frame in code with 3JS, designs the sound, and checks a draft before rendering the final version from your notes.

sections.title: terminal-mac
paragraphs: Terminal Mac gives AI agents their own separate Mac OS desktop to work on running as a virtual machine on your Apple Silicon Mac. It uses Apple's own virtualization framework, so the guest is a real copy of Mac OS. You watch and steer it right from your terminal. Agents get MCP tools to take screenshots, click, drag, scroll, and type all inside the guest.

sections.title: latch
paragraphs: Latch is a tiny contract for how an AI agent asks a service to do something for real, like place an order using one card and a single web endpoint. The service publishes a card describing what it can do. The agent asks for a quote which comes with a fingerprint of exactly what will happen. A person approves that exact fingerprint and only then can the agent commit getting a receipt back.

sections.title: gputaskman
paragraphs: GPU Taskman is an htop for your GPU from Scott Hansselman and it shows what's actually inside your graphics card, not just how full it is. It runs in the terminal on Windows with Nvidia cards built in Python with textual. For each program, it shows how much GPU memory it uses, what it's running on, and how much has spilled over into regular RAM. Charts track memory, power, and temperature over time. sections.title: kairos
paragraphs: risk decisions as activity happens. Send it events like login, orders, or payouts, and it can approve them, request extra verification, or flag them for review along with the reasons behind the decision. It also connects to coding agents through MCP, so they can help build workflows and test different risk models.

sections.title: equal
paragraphs: equal records real API traffic once, then lets you work against it offline, all from one small Go binary. Run it as a local proxy in front of an API and it saves every request in response to a file, hiding secrets as it goes. Later, it replays those exact responses without ever touching the real service. And any request it never saw gets a clear 404 instead of a guess. It can turn a recording into an open API spec. sections.title: runner-up
paragraphs: GitHub, sees which jobs are waiting, and hands each one to a free slot on one of your computers over SSH. That slot spins up a clean environment with Docker, a Linux VM, a Mac VM, or HyperV, runs one job and throws it away.

sections.title: djs
paragraphs: DJS is a compact JavaScript and TypeScript engine in Rust made to run inside web assembly and it now powers the code in the PI coding agent in place of quickJS. In code mode, the AI writes small scripts that call tools and work with the results and DJs runs them. Its trick is that the entire engine sits in one block of memory. So you can freeze it at any instruction and save it by copying bytes.

sections.title: latent-sparse-attention
paragraphs: Latent sparse attention is a research project aimed at helping AI models handle extremely long inputs more efficiently. It groups information into clusters so the model can select relevant parts instead of checking everything in detail. The researchers report faster attention in their long context tests while keeping accuracy close to the original models.

sections.title: tucano
paragraphs: Tucano brings your AI agents together in a desktop app that feels like a team chat. Give each agent a role and they can handwork between each other. So one investigates a bug, another fixes it and a third reviews the result. It works with tools like clawed code and codecs, connects to apps through MCP and lets you approve sensitive actions before they happen.

sections.title: quiet-md
paragraphs: Quiet MD is a local first notes app for Mac OS and Windows written in Rust on GPUi which draws the interface on the GPU. It handles rich text with to-dos, code blocks, latex, tables, and columns. Notes live as XML files in a folder on your computer with markdown and PDF export. The author reports typing stays under 6 milliseconds per frame in a million character document.

sections.title: poki
paragraphs: Pokey lets an AI agent use a real iPhone without jailbreaking it. Pair your phone with a Mac, connect an agent like Claude Code or Codeex, and ask it to perform tasks in your apps. It uses a local MCP server to control the device, while screen contents go to your configured AI model. There's also a standalone agent you can use from the terminal.

sections.title: sand3d
paragraphs: SAN 3D lets you build 3D models with short Python programs designed to be easy for AI models to write and people to read. Describe an object part by part, add details like holes and rounded edges, and even give it moving joints. It uses Blender underneath and can export models for the web, game engines, 3D printing, and robot simulators.

sections.title: MagoStudio
paragraphs: Mag Studio is an open-source AI video editor that lets you work on your own computer. Start with a script and build out shots and storyboards, or bring in footage to restyle, relight, or edit selected areas with masks. You can render locally on your GPU through Comfy UI, or use paid cloud models when you need them. Your projects stay on your machine.

sections.title: asm
paragraphs: ASM is a package registry and command line tool for assembly language. You can create projects, build, run, and test them and pin source dependencies in a lock file. Packages come with size and Shaw 256 checks, and every release carries its source and verification results. It runs on Linux and Apple Silicon Max. What stands out is that the tool managing assembly packages is written in assembly itself. SlideSense is a Mac OS menu bar app written in Swift that turns the edges of your

sections.title: slidesense
paragraphs: MacBook trackpad into sliders. Slide along the left edge for brightness and the right edge for volume with haptic ticks and an onscreen display at each step. There's a precise quarterep mode, a double tap corner for mute, and a media strip along the bottom. It needs no hardware and never touches the network.

sections.title: kiri
paragraphs: Kiri is a lightweight container runtime for Mac, Windows, and Linux that works with your existing Docker commands and images. It runs containers in a small Linux virtual machine or directly on the Linux kernel and puts your containers, images, and volumes in a native window. You can also spin up a local Kubernetes cluster or create a Linux machine from the command line.

sections.title: Winc
paragraphs: Wink is a desktop code editor written in Rust with its own rendering engine. It handles multiple cursors, syntax highlighting, quick go-to definition without a language server, and previews for markdown, images, and spreadsheets. Git is built in with sidebyside diffs, hunk staging, blame, and a commit graph, plus an integrated terminal. It runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

sections.title: open-bot-avatar
paragraphs: Openbot Avatar gives your AI agents a face with just a little JSON. define a shape and where the eyes go, and its renderer turns that into an animated character that can follow your cursor, look thoughtful, or show a happy expression. There's also an editor for picking colors and creating your own designs, plus a gallery of avatars to start with.

sections.title: NextTransformer
paragraphs: Next, Transformer is an open-source research framework for comparing different language model architectures. It trains approaches like sparse attention, linear attention, and recurrent models on the same data with matched computing budgets so researchers can compare their results under the same rules. You can explore training curves and model cards in the browser or add your own architecture to the benchmark.

sections.title: statechart-art
paragraphs: This project explains state charts through the daily life of a boba shop. One chart follows an order from the line to your hand, while another shows the barista and teapot working at the same time. Each illustration is drawn in code to look like pen and colored pencil and backed by a model that's checked for broken rules, including one that catches old pearls being served.

sections.title: uni-robot-agent
paragraphs: Uni Robot Agent gives AI agents a shared set of tools for working with robots across different simulated environments. You can give it a task like stacking bowls, watch the robot's camera feeds and tool calls on a dashboard and replay the run afterward. It supports codecs and clawed code runtimes with physical robot integrations planned for a future release.

sections.title: blank-page
paragraphs: Blank page helps when you know you need a motion graphic but have no idea what it should look like. Give this clawed code or codec skill a oneline idea and it finds visual references, explores motion, and turns it into a detailed creative prompt with a sequence of beats. You can review its choices, make changes, and hand the prompt to an agent to create the video. Kubai icons is a clawed skill that draws icons in one consistent style built on a JavaScript

sections.title: kubai-icons
paragraphs: engine and SVG. You describe an icon and it comes back either animated on hover or exported as a static file in one of seven pallets. It ships with 66 example icons and a live gallery. Headless Chrome renders every new icon and compares it against the set before you keep it.

sections.title: CardboardXR
paragraphs: Cardboard XR is a Unity app that brings classic phone in a viewer VR up to date using Arcore and Arkit through AR Foundation. On top of split screen stereo, it adds six degrees of freedom head tracking, camera pass through, surface detection, and hand tracking with pinch and grab. Demos include air painting, a rhythm game, and a pass through portal.

sections.title: sshyard
paragraphs: SSH Wired brings your remote servers, files, and AI assistance into one desktop app. Open multiple SSH sessions in tabs or split panes, then manage files over SFTP right beside your terminal. You can connect an AI assistant for each host to help run commands and edit files with different access modes to choose from. It works on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

sections.title: ImmichGallery
paragraphs: Image Gallery is a native Mac OS app for browsing your self-hosted image photo server written in Swift UI by an independent developer. Your timeline, albums, people, places, and live photos all open in a proper Mac window with smart search, OCR, and uploads that skip duplicates. Quick look, drag and drop shortcuts and tabs work the way you'd expect. Live Live Player is a

sections.title: player
paragraphs: lightweight browser library for animated 2.5D characters built on WebGL2 with no dependencies in its 34 kilob core. A few lines of code put a character on a page in an app or in a stream overlay. It lip syncs to your microphone, audio, or video and follows your face through the webcam with media pipe. VRM models and PNG tubers play through the same API and camera images never leave your device.

sections.title: atlas-filemanager
paragraphs: Atlas is a native file manager for Windows written in Rust and drawn on the GPU with GPUi. It gives you five views including Miller columns plus tabs, split panes and a command pallet. Search is indexed, archives open like folders and files convert locally between image, video, audio and document formats. It also reaches Google Drive, One Drive, and network shares.

sections.title: Stroq
paragraphs: Stro is a local action firewall for AI coding agents written in Typescript. It scans everything the agent reads from files and web pages to command output and MCP results. If something looks malicious, the session is marked as tainted and risky moves like pushing to an outside repo, reading secrets, or sending data out get blocked or need your approval.

sections.title: gauge-cli
paragraphs: Gage CLI is an open-source command line tool that tests how well coding agents can use your skills, CLIs, and SDKs. It spins up real sessions with clawed codecs inside Docker and flags where the agent gets stuck. You can then try a fix and compare the new batch against the baseline before you ship. The full loop runs locally, and you don't need an account.
